llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Attio connector that can read and change CRM data through OOMOL, with clear instructions to confirm write and delete actions first.

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose is to operate Attio through the OOMOL oo CLI, including reads, creates, updates, upserts, and deletes; that is high-impact CRM access but it is explicitly stated and aligned with the Attio integration purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions scope actions to the attio connector, require live schema inspection, distinguish read/write/destructive actions, and require user confirmation before state-changing or destructive operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: First-time setup may install the oo CLI using OOMOL-hosted install scripts and requires OOMOL sign-in or Attio connection only when authentication fails; this is disclosed but users should be comfortable with OOMOL as the intermediary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Allowed tool access is narrowly declared as Bash(oo *), and the requested Attio/OOMOL access is proportionate to the stated connector workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill relies on a persistent OOMOL account connection and server-side injected Attio credentials, but it does not define hidden background jobs, local indexing, or automatic persistence beyond the expected connector account setup.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let OOMOL mediate access to your Attio workspace. Review the exact payload before approving create, update, upsert, or delete actions, and make sure the connected Attio credentials have only the scopes you actually need.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues; artifact review found no hidden instructions or purpose-mismatched behavior.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean across engines and does not conflict with the coherent single-file skill artifact.
[staticScan] expected: Static scan reported no findings; the inspected SKILL.md contains disclosed connector usage and safety guidance for write and delete operations.
